terms.gloss: a career, a walk of life
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.117: in quō genere vītae
Cic. Off. 1.120: in dēligendō genere vītae, in choosing a career
terms.comment: Cicero’s term for the life one chooses in early youth (Off. 1.117–121).

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.117: certō genere cursūque vīvendī
Traupman 180: cursus honōrum, a political career
terms.comment: The political career, the ladder of offices, is cursus honōrum (cf. Cic. Fam. 3.11.2, Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: in prīmīs autem cōnstituendum est, quōs nōs et quālēs esse velīmus et in quō genere vītae, quae dēlīberātiō est omnium difficillima
phrases.english: above all we must decide who and what kind of people we want to be, and in what career; and that is the hardest decision of all

sources: Lewis & Short: genus · Lewis & Short: cursus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 180.
Cicero, De officiis, checked against the Latin Library texts (CLTK mirror) (9 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
